paras: The Meridian race riot was a disturbance at Meridian, Mississippi, reported in August 1900 as 'something of a race riot' that followed a Black man's resistance to arrest. It is known only from a single sentence in a Mississippi weekly's state-news column, which gave no names, date, acts or casualties.

According to The Leader's 'State News' column of August 22, 1900, the riot occurred 'as the result of a negro resisting arrest' at Meridian. The item did not say when the arrest took place, who attempted it, what the man was accused of, or what happened once the disturbance began. No deaths, injuries or arrests were mentioned.
No follow-up report, inquest or prosecution connected to the disturbance appears in the coverage.

The Leader ran the report as one line among routine Mississippi notes, set between items on a West Point barrel factory and a lynching in Holmes County. Its wording, 'something of a race riot', played down the scale of the event, and it placed the cause on the Black man who resisted arrest rather than on any crowd. No other white paper and no Black paper was found to have reported the incident.
